bullets.title: 反面教師
bullets.note:
(**[_**hanmen kyoushi**_](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%8F%8D%E9%9D%A2%E6%95%99%E5%B8%AB)**)**. Some languages have elegant ways of capturing things that require a sentence in English. [_Saudade_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudade) in Portuguese is close to this. [_Komorebi_](https://www.morethantokyo.com/komorebi-japanese-word/) in Japanese certainly checks the box. Now I can add _hanmen kyoushi_ to my ever-growing list.  
​  
“反面教師 (はんめん きょうし, hanmen kyoushi, 反面教员 in Chinese) is a Chinese/Japanese idiom that means ‘an example of bad people/things that you should not follow/imitate.’” ([Source](https://takashionary.com/hanmen-kyoushi-meaning/))  
​  
Think of it as “opposite teacher.” Deep bow to Kristy for putting this on my radar.
